purpose: Use protest/assembly dates in Kazakhstan as natural experiments for testing whether network restrictions are event-conditioned, geographically localized, and reproducible. This artifact does not attribute Russian command or Russian equipment.
core_rule: PROTEST_CORRELATION strengthens evidence of deliberate domestic network control, but does not establish Russian control-plane attribution.

timeline.network_observation: RSF reported multiple news sites inaccessible from dawn; Facebook, Telegram, YouTube and Instagram disconnected around midday; some mobile users also reported Internet problems.
timeline.source: RSF — Heavy Internet censorship in Kazakhstan

timeline.event: Anti-government protests in multiple cities calling for release of political prisoners
timeline.network_observation: Access Now reported shutdowns in Almaty and Nur-Sultan approximately 14:00-17:00 local time; IODA measurements independently indicated disruptions in the same period. Reports also existed for Atyrau but lacked confirming measurements.

Localized mobile throttling began in western Kazakhstan on Jan 2 as protests started; messenger access problems followed; by Jan 4-5 disruptions escalated to nationwide blackout. NetBlocks measured national connectivity near 5% of ordinary levels. Access Now recorded corroboration from Cloudflare, IODA and Google traffic data. Restoration was selective/intermittent, with government-controlled news and banking among early restored services.
timeline.source: Freedom House + NetBlocks + Access Now + Cloudflare/IODA/Google references

timeline.event: Almaty rally marking first anniversary of January 2022 events
timeline.network_observation: Freedom House reports local throttling during the rally.

timeline.event: Oil-worker protests / solidarity mobilization in Zhanaozen and Astana
timeline.network_observation: Local reporting documented Internet shutdown and degraded phone service in Zhanaozen as crowds gathered; reports placed shutdown near the central square and noted weak/VPN-only access in some areas.
timeline.source: KIBHR/Exclusive/Vlast/Eurasianet; also summarized by Freedom House

timeline.network_observation: Internet/mobile problems appeared during the protest, especially among Activ/Kcell users; regional complaints followed. Local reporting states connectivity stabilized after the protest ended on May 22. Freedom House records throttling during the Kulsary rallies.
timeline.source: Freedom House 2024 + Orda.kz + Vlast + Adil Soz

timeline.network_observation: KazTAG reported provider blocking after critical constitutional-reform coverage; HRW/ODIHR documented pressure on critics. A later OONI-derived signal showed elevated interference around March 24, after the March 15 referendum, but this is not yet tied to a specific protest event or ASN/path.

timeline.event: Pre-election period before Aug 23 parliamentary election
timeline.network_observation: Large Kazakhstan-specific Telegram outage was reported across several regions while no global Telegram outage was reported. No verified protest-day correlation has yet been found for this date.

2022_dpi_correction.previous_risk: Some secondary reporting describes the January 2022 attempted selective filtering as use of Russian DPI technology.
2022_dpi_correction.corrected_claim: Available technical reporting indicates Kazakhstan attempted DPI-based selective blocking analogous to Russia's sovereign-Internet method, but the installed DPI equipment identified in reporting was from Israeli vendor Allot. Russian equipment deployment for this specific event is NOT established.

satisfied: repeat protest-conditioned network restrictions across multiple years
geographic localization in multiple local protest cases
clear foreign-service reachability impact during nationwide blackout
missing_for_red: current 2026 ASN/path localization for the same event
matched alternate-path/bypass control for a current incident
specific US-service nexus demonstrated at measurement level rather than inferred from broad outage
device/vendor/control-plane linkage for the current event

next_pass: Search OONI raw measurements around 2026 protest/referendum/election windows by ASN and test_name.
Search RIPE Atlas/IODA/Cloudflare Radar for matching localized anomalies on the same dates.
Compare protest locations with operator footprints (Kcell/Activ, Tele2/Altel, Beeline, Kazakhtelecom) and ASN-level behavior.
Separate DNS blocking, TCP/TLS interference, mobile throttling and full route withdrawal into distinct mechanisms.
Do not upgrade CISA gate solely from political-event timing.
